title: LeetCode Problems
description: Interview-style algorithm problems with an online editor and test cases.
startWith: Choose Easy array, string, and hash-map problems. Write Python first; explain time and space complexity.
accessNote: Free problems are available; Premium unlocks additional questions and features. An account is useful for submissions.

title: NeetCode Roadmap
description: A structured route through coding-interview patterns, including Arrays & Hashing.
startWith: Start with Arrays & Hashing. Attempt a problem before watching its explanation.
accessNote: The roadmap and practice lists have free content; Pro courses and features are separate.

title: Python Track
description: Python exercises focused on language concepts, readable solutions, and test-driven practice.
startWith: Practise dictionaries, collections, and functions to get comfortable coding from a blank file.
accessNote: Free Python track. An account is needed to save work and use track features.

title: Python Challenges
description: Small Python challenges covering strings, sets, collections, classes, and debugging.
startWith: Use the basic data types, sets, and collections sections as warm-ups before timed problems.
accessNote: Sign-in may be needed to submit and save challenge progress.

title: Machine Learning Crash Course
description: Modular explanations and exercises for regression, classification, data, and model evaluation.
startWith: Study classification metrics, overfitting, and dataset splits; explain each concept in your own words.
accessNote: Public learning material. Some exercises use a notebook environment.

title: Intro to Machine Learning
description: An applied introduction to building and validating a first machine-learning model.
startWith: Work through model validation and underfitting/overfitting, then reproduce a notebook locally.
accessNote: Kaggle Learn is free; an account may be required for interactive exercises.

title: Machine Learning in Python
description: A careful introduction to predictive pipelines, preprocessing, cross-validation, and interpreting results.
startWith: Start with the predictive modeling pipeline and model evaluation. Keep preprocessing inside the training workflow.
accessNote: Public lessons and notebooks. The hosted MOOC has optional enrollment for additional course features.

title: Learn the Basics
description: Official tutorials following a complete workflow: tensors, datasets, models, autograd, and optimization.
startWith: Follow tensors, autograd, and the optimization loop. Rewrite one tiny training loop without copying.
accessNote: Tutorials are free. You can run examples locally or through supported notebook links.

title: Dive into Deep Learning
description: A mathematical, code-based textbook covering neural networks, optimization, attention, and transformers.
startWith: Read automatic differentiation and forward/backward propagation alongside the PyTorch examples.
accessNote: Free online book and code. Local or cloud computing is needed to run exercises.

title: Deep Learning for Coders — Online Book
description: The fast.ai book links its explanations to notebooks you can read and run.
startWith: Begin with the MNIST basics chapter and compare its model-building approach with your PyTorch loop.
accessNote: The online book is free; print editions and optional cloud compute may cost money.

title: LLM Course
description: Learn transformers, tokenizers, datasets, model inference, and fine-tuning through the Hugging Face ecosystem.
startWith: Start with transformer architectures and tokenization before fine-tuning. Practise describing model types.
accessNote: The course is free. Accounts or computing resources may be needed for hands-on activities.

title: AI Agents Course
description: Agent foundations, tools, frameworks, agentic RAG, and evaluation with practical assignments.
startWith: Review tools and agent fundamentals, then try the Agentic RAG unit for your Atlas AI project.
accessNote: Course material is free. A free Hugging Face account supports hands-on activities; external compute/API usage can vary.

title: Generative AI for Beginners
description: Open learning material for building generative-AI applications with practical examples.
startWith: Read the introductory and prompt-design material, then build a small grounded-answering experiment.
accessNote: Lessons are free to read. Running examples can require provider accounts and incur model/API charges.

title: Introduction to LangGraph — Python
description: Learn graph-based agent workflows, state, memory, and human-in-the-loop patterns.
startWith: Begin with simple graphs, state schemas, and reducers. Use the transcripts and notebooks if you prefer reading.
accessNote: The course is free; registration may be required. Model calls and optional hosted services can have separate costs.

title: Interactive SQL Lessons
description: Short interactive lessons for SELECT, filtering, joins, aggregation, and data modification.
startWith: Practise JOINs and GROUP BY, then explain how a query maps to your booking or complaint database.

title: FastAPI Tutorial — User Guide
description: Official examples for request validation, response codes, authentication, databases, and testing.
startWith: Build a tiny complaint endpoint with validation and correct HTTP status codes, then add tests.
accessNote: Documentation is free. Run the sample API locally with Codex or Claude Code.
